paper.title: GrIPS: Gradient-free, Edit-based Instruction Search for Prompting Large Language Models
paper.central_claim: GrIPS, a gradient-free phrase-level edit search over instructions scored on a small labeled set, improves task instructions for LLMs including API-only models; it outperforms manual rewriting and example-prompt search at matched budget and is comparable to select gradient-based tuning.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: subagent runtime exposes no receipt to the worker; model identity is the configured claude-kimi type only. Full text incl. Appendices A-G read.

sections_read: App A-G (tables of searched instructions skimmed)

evidence.quote: manual rewriting is time-consuming and requires subjective interpretation, while gradient-based tuning can be extremely computationally demanding for large models and may not be feasible for API-based models
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap: manual rewriting is costly/subjective, gradient tuning is infeasible for API models.

evidence.quote: maintaining the human-readability of the resulting instructions
evidence.support_explanation: Claimed advantage over gradient-based prompt tuning: human-readable output.

evidence.quote: it is possible that the prompts that most improve model performance are semantically confusing to humans in some ways
evidence.support_explanation: Premise that useful instructions need not be coherent.

evidence.quote: Qualitatively, we show our edits can simplify instructions and at times make them incoherent but nonetheless improve accuracy.
evidence.support_explanation: Result: edits can be incoherent yet improve accuracy; tension with the readability claim.

evidence.quote: The search is guided by model performance on a small pool of examples that are not a part of the test set
evidence.support_explanation: Score set S (|S|=100) is disjoint from the test set.

evidence.quote: we also include the entropy of model predictions in the score function to promote edited instructions that generate diverse labels
evidence.support_explanation: Score = balanced accuracy + alpha*entropy of predicted-label distribution (alpha=10).

evidence.quote: If the score of the best candidate exceeds the score of the current base instruction, then that candidate is assigned as the base in the next iteration. Otherwise, the search continues with the same base instruction.
evidence.support_explanation: Acceptance rule: strict improvement on the score set, otherwise keep the incumbent (implicit rollback).

evidence.quote: The search stops when the score on
evidence.support_explanation: Patience/early-stop rule (P=2, n=10).

evidence.quote: Addition ( add ). We sample a phrase deleted in previous iterations
evidence.support_explanation: Edit operators delete/swap/paraphrase/add act on phrases of the instruction; no LLM variation and no error diagnosis.

evidence.quote: CRF-based constituency parser
evidence.support_explanation: Phrases from a CRF constituency parser; edits are structure-aware but blind to errors.

evidence.quote: We set number of edit operations per candidate l = 1 l=1 , number of candidates per iteration m = 5 m=5 , number of iterations n = 10 n=10 , and patience P = 2 P=2 . Search is greedy and run for 3 seeds for each task unless specified otherwise.
evidence.support_explanation: Hyperparameters and 3 seeds.

evidence.quote: the test sets consist of 300 random samples per task
evidence.support_explanation: Main-result test sets: 300 samples/task, 8 tasks.

evidence.quote: all other analysis and ablation experiments in § 5 are evaluated on subsets of 100 test examples per task
evidence.support_explanation: Ablations and comparisons use only 100 test examples/task (noisy).

evidence.quote: In all test sets, data is sampled such that the sets are as balanced as possible
evidence.support_explanation: Test sets are balanced only when data allow; four of the eight tasks have >90% skew in the source data.

evidence.support_explanation: Gain correlates with the model's instruction sensitivity (r>0.7 for two models).

GPT-2 XL is below the 59.83 majority baseline both before (49.54) and after (58.90) search, and babbage after search (60.09) is within noise of the majority baseline; test sets remain skewed for four tasks. Part of the "improvement" may be label-bias correction (the entropy term rewards diverse predicted labels) rather than task understanding; predicted-label distributions on test are not reported.

Searched all sections: there is no random-edit / best-of-N-without-iteration control and no calibration baseline (e.g. contextual calibration); the only search-internal comparisons are greedy vs beam vs simulated annealing and edit-op ablations on GPT-2 XL.
Proposal and gating use the same score set S (|S|=100); the held-out test set is separate, so the commit rule is not disjoint but reported results are.

signatures.object: The natural-language task instruction (the "definition" field) inside a fixed prompt template for a classification task; one instruction per task/model/seed.
signatures.information: Search sees score-set labels (100 examples, balanced accuracy + prediction entropy) via label log-probabilities; test labels unseen; no error traces; API-only access.
signatures.operation: Split instruction into phrases (CRF constituency parser); sample l=1 edit (delete, swap, paraphrase with PEGASUS, add back a deleted phrase) for m=5 candidates; score; accept best if score strictly improves; patience 2, <=10 iterations; optional beam/SA.
signatures.output: Edited instruction (often shorter, sometimes incoherent) used for all test inputs of that task.
signatures.conditions: Instruction-following LM (InstructGPT) works best; needs 20-100 labeled examples; classification with label probabilities.
signatures.feedback: Score-set accuracy/entropy of the model with the candidate instruction.
signatures.selection_rule: Strict improvement over incumbent on the score set; otherwise keep incumbent; early stop by patience; beam keeps top-B.
signatures.persistence: Final instruction string (per task/model/seed); no cross-task library.
signatures.later_use: Applied to held-out test examples; the search is rerun per task/model.
signatures.claimed_effect: +2.4 to +9.4 points average accuracy; beats manual rewriting and example search at matched queries; comparable to some gradient tuning.
signatures.failure_boundary: GPT-2 XL returns original instruction on 3 tasks; gains scale with model instruction sensitivity and score-set size; cannot add new information; classification only; not tested on largest model.

gap.author_gap: Manual instruction rewriting is slow and subjective and assumes human-coherent instructions; gradient-based prompt tuning is expensive, impossible for API-only models and not human-readable.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and well sourced for the 2021-22 literature (Mishra et al. rewriting guidelines, prefix/prompt tuning, AutoPrompt, exemplar search, paraphrase-based template search). The stated readability advantage is partly undercut by the paper's own finding of incoherent edits.
lineage: Prompt search: Jiang 2020, Gao 2021 paraphrase templates; Lu 2022, Kumar & Talukdar 2021 exemplar order/selection
gap.closest_adjacent: Exemplar-prompt search and template paraphrasing (same gradient-free, black-box setting), implemented as a matched-query baseline.
gap.residue: Edit operators cannot add new information; gains are model- and task-dependent.
gap.stakes: Improve API-model prompts at small labeled-data cost.
gap.method_response: Greedy/beam local search over phrase-level edits scored on a small labeled set.
gap.remaining_gap: Generative tasks, new-information edits, largest models, interpretation of incoherent edits.
unresolved: Later LLM-proposed prompt search (APE-like) is out of scope for the pinned v2 and not checked.

rs_pattern.reason: The operation is greedy/beam hill-climbing over discrete phrase edits of a prompt with a black-box score set (a gradient-free local search). None of the 15 RS ideation patterns defines this operation. Nearest candidates read and rejected: reframe_as_solvable_object (prompt tuning is recast as local search but no new object/correspondence theorem is introduced, and hill-climbing is not a mature solver imported with guarantees), assumption_audit_and_pivot (partial pivot on the "instructions must be coherent" assumption in Sec 5.7, but there is no audit/relaxation derivation), architectural_operator_substitution (gradient-free search substitutes the gradient operator but no preservation property is shown). No sub-card is claimed (C-cards are ML-subfield clusters).
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: improves accuracy on API models without gradients for some tasks; the readability goal is not met in many cases.

expectations.reason: Score set disjoint from test; main results on 300 test examples per task. Caveat: hyperparameter tuning data unspecified.
Cost formula and dollar costs reported; example-search baseline at the same maximum number of queries.

expectations.applies_when: Claim that the search adds value.
expectations.reason: No-search and matched-query baselines exist; no random-edit or best-of-N control and no calibration baseline.
3 seeds (5 for Inst+Ex), bootstrap CIs and significance tests; gradient baselines are single-split.
Gate uses the same score set that proposals are scored on (no separate commit split); the final test is separate.
Entropy bonus is a proxy for calibration; majority-label comparison suggests part of the gain may be label-bias correction.

expectations.source_strength: single_source (this paper) - listed as practice, not as shared consensus
expectations.applies_when: A model may have seen the benchmark.
expectations.reason: FLAN-T5 flagged explicitly; other models are non-instruction-tuned or InstructGPT of unknown training.

expectations.applies_when: Baselines are implemented by the authors.
expectations.reason: Manual rewriting was done by the authors (5 h) and gradient baselines are compared at different compute.

claims.text: GrIPS improves average accuracy: GPT-2 XL +9.36, InstructGPT babbage +4.29, curie +2.36 (8 Natural-Instructions classification tasks).
claims.setting: Instruction-only prompts; 3 seeds x 8 tasks; 300 test examples/task.
claims.selection_vs_test: Search on a 100-example score set; test is separate.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Significant average gains on this task set; two of three models end near the majority-label level; per-task wins are 4/8, 7/8, 5/8.

claims.text: GrIPS outperforms manual rewriting and exemplar-prompt search while controlling compute and data.
claims.baseline_control: Authors' manual rewrite; example search at the same maximum queries.
claims.result_denominator: Manual: 47.70/55.50/57.87 vs GrIPS 53.68/57.79/59.37; example search 56.00/56.25/57.75 (GrIPS better only for InstructGPT).
claims.allowed_conclusion: Matched-query advantage on InstructGPT models by 1.5-1.6 points; GPT-2 XL example search wins; manual baseline is the authors' own.

claims.text: GrIPS is comparable to select gradient-based tuning (GPT-2 XL).
claims.setting: Fine-tuning, adapters, prefix-tuning on the 80% train split of the score set.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Greedy GrIPS is below finetuning/adapters; beam search (about 5x queries) exceeds them; compute is not matched.

claims.text: Searched instructions can be incoherent yet more accurate; gains hold with task-agnostic initialisation and shrink with fewer score examples.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Qualitative only; the readability advantage claimed in the introduction does not hold in many searched instructions.

assessment.evidence_level_note: The searched instruction (retained non-weight artifact) improves held-out test accuracy of the same task; no improver-level claim.
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Greedy phrase-edit search against a 100-example score set yields instructions that raise held-out accuracy on 8 binary classification tasks and beats matched-query exemplar search on InstructGPT models; part of the gain may be label-bias correction and the readability advantage is not supported.

G.reason: Gap is specific (API-only black-box, subjective manual rewriting, unreadable gradient prompts) and positioned against rewriting, prompt tuning and prompt-search neighbors with a matched-query implementation; the unexamined assumption that readability is preserved weakens the stated residue.

M.reason: Mechanism is simple and explicit (local edits, strict-improvement acceptance, entropy-augmented score) with ablations explaining pieces; the readability rationale conflicts with the incoherent results and the reason gains occur (calibration vs semantics) is open.

X.reason: Full pseudocode for greedy/beam/SA, operators, parser, hyperparameters, stopping and failure behavior (return original), costs and conditions of applicability are reconstructable; incumbent is retained unless strictly improved (implicit rollback).

E.measurement.reason: Accuracy with label log-probabilities on gold labels and CIs; but test sets are partly skewed, GPT-2 XL and babbage end near the 59.83 majority baseline, ablations use 100 test examples/task, and balanced-accuracy/predicted-label distributions are not reported on test.

E.causality.reason: Baselines at matched queries (example search), no-search, manual rewriting, gradient methods, plus op/entropy ablations; missing random-edit/best-of-N and calibration controls, authors' own manual baseline, unmatched compute for gradient comparison.

E.holdout.reason: Score set disjoint from test; large-enough test (300/task); contamination flagged for FLAN-T5; transfer across models/tasks not claimed. Hyperparameters tuned on unspecified data and single benchmark family.

E.statistics.reason: 3-5 seeds, bootstrap CIs, p<0.05 tests, per-task win counts and failure cases reported; ablations on 100 test examples lack intervals.

E.cost.reason: Cost formula, dollar cost per search run and total, matched-query comparison with example search; gradient baselines and beam search not compute-matched.

status_reason: Full pinned text read; outside the 15 RS ideation patterns (reason recorded), still fully scored.
rationale: Solid B-class prompt optimizer: explicit acceptance rule, disjoint score/test sets, CIs, costs, matched-query baseline. Weaknesses: results near majority baseline, no random/calibration control, authors' own manual baseline, readability claim contradicted.
